**Proposed mechanism:** c.1824C>T (p.Gly609Gly) (rs137852742) —DISRUPTS→ LMNA (HGNC:6877); LMNA (HGNC:6877) —LEADS_TO→ Progeria (HP:0000975); ATM (HGNC:79) —DISRUPTS→ DNA damage response (GO:0006974); DNA damage response (GO:0006974) —DECREASES→ Proteasome degradation pathway (GO:0043161); LMNA (HGNC:6877) —DECREASES→ Proteasome degradation pathway (GO:0043161); Proteasome degradation pathway (GO:0043161) —LEADS_TO→ Oropharyngeal cancer predisposition (HP:0030128). A specific gain-of-function mutation in LMNA (c.1824C>T, p.Gly609Gly) leads to Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and the accumulation of toxic progerin. This toxic protein may interfere with normal cellular processes, including protein degradation via the proteasome. In familial cutaneous telangiectasia and oropharyngeal predisposition cancer syndrome, loss-of-function mutations in genes like ATM disrupt the DNA damage response, which can indirectly impair cellular proteostasis and proteasome function. Both pathways converge on a dysregulated proteasome degradation pathway, leading to cellular dysfunction and predisposition to oropharyngeal cancer.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in LMNA do not affect proteasome function or that ATM mutations do not have any downstream effect on proteasome-mediated degradation in cellular models. _(variant: rs137852742)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared impact on the proteasome degradation pathway could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both progeroid syndromes and cancer predisposition syndromes, potentially involving proteasome modulators or agents that enhance protein clearance.
